title: This Week in Evermarch: The Chronicle Begins
excerpt: Active mining received a major hands-on overhaul, with drag mining, chest rewards, TNT, clearer damage states, mobile improvements, and a long list of save and interface fixes.

body.text: Welcome to the first weekly Evermarch update. It has been a busy week: 17 tracked improvements were completed across active mining, saves, offline progress, mobile play, inventory safety, and interface polish.

items: Active mining is now truly hands-on: hold and drag across the mine face to keep striking blocks as you move.
Breaking mining blocks can reveal chests. Chests stack, can be opened in batches, and currently award TNT.
TNT can now be used from the mining screen to blast every visible block and collect the rewards.
Blocks now show clearer square-chip damage states, material rubble when broken, and a chest-found presentation instead of subtle line effects.
The mining board has been rebuilt for small screens so the mine face gets the space, depth rail, and labels it needs.
Active mining no longer uses rhythm multipliers or the old layer progress bar. Your manual strikes are the focus.
Mining experience is now paced at the intended 2.5x routine-mining rate, with a strike cadence cap and accurate fractional XP carry-over.
Cloud restores preserve the original save time, so the Welcome Back summary correctly reflects time spent away.
The save picker now has a visible refresh action to recheck both device and cloud progress, plus clear feedback when a cloud restore succeeds or fails.
The return-from-idle modal has a solid, readable Continue action that stays clear even when its content scrolls.
Native alerts and browser confirmation prompts have been replaced with game-native modals.
#1 — Inventory summaries now hide Filtered Value when All is selected and let the remaining values use the space naturally.
#2 — The inventory sort selector now has a readable Evermarch-styled surface, text, options, hover state, and focus state.
#3 — All But 1 is now a safe one-shot sale calculation that protects the last item, respects a manually entered 0, and never resets that choice during routine updates.
#4 — Restore to device now restores a cloud save correctly and clearly reports loading, success, or failure.
#5 — The mobile save-selection header now keeps its back action, Evermarch title, and player name on one compact row.
#6 — A save will no longer open or resume without an explicit Continue action from the player.
#7 — Restoring a backup now keeps its original timestamp, fixing incorrect Welcome Back time and reward calculations.
#9 — Hold-and-drag mining now follows the block beneath your pointer, continues after a block breaks, and stops when you release or leave the mine face.
#10 — Active mining now fits a phone screen properly, with a square mine face, matched depth rail, visible depth labels, and no wasted Mining mode card.
#11 — Rhythm multipliers and the redundant mining layer bar are gone in favour of direct manual block breaking.
#12 — Mining damage now uses three clear square-chip patterns with staged progression, rubble, and no diagonal or rotational crack glyphs.
#13 — Mining chests now spawn, enter inventory, open in batches of up to 1,000, and award one or two TNT each.
#14 — TNT is now a functional mining tool with a blast animation that breaks the visible mine face.
#15 — Browser alert, confirm, and prompt dialogs have been replaced with consistent Evermarch modals.
#16 — Active-mining XP is now capped and balanced against routine mining instead of rewarding uncontrolled rapid tapping.
#17 — The character-selection page now includes a refresh control for checking current device and cloud saves.
#20 — The Welcome Back modal now uses an opaque, separated Continue button that remains readable over scrollable content.

body.text: The screenshots below show the result of this week's work: a clear save selector, an offline-progress return summary, and the active Rune Essence mining face with depth tracking, block damage, mastery, and an ore unlock rail.
This is the beginning of the weekly Evermarch journal. Future updates will keep the same focus: what changed, what is new, and how the game is evolving for players.
